title: A History of Christianity
subtitle: From the Second Temple to the Present
description: A spoken history of Christianity in forty chapters, from Second Temple Judaism and the historical Jesus to the present: doctrine, heresy and empire, East and West, medieval Christendom, Reformation, mission and empire, and the twentieth century. Seasons follow the eight Parts; the annexes on saints and holidays are bonus episodes.
author: Study

episodes.title: 1. Second Temple Judaism and the Historical Jesus: What Can Be Known
episodes.description: The Problem of Sources; Methods and Their Limits; Second Temple Judaism: The World Jesus Inhabited; Jesus of Nazareth: A Sketch Within the Evidence.

episodes.title: 2. Paul, the Gentile Mission, and the Earliest Communities
episodes.description: The Earliest Jerusalem Community; Saul of Tarsus; The Gentile Mission and Its Theological Logic; The Shape of the Pauline Mission.

episodes.title: 3. Persecution, Apologetics, and the Church Within the Roman Empire
episodes.description: A Movement Without Legal Standing; The Pattern of Persecution: Local, Sporadic, and Later Systematic; The Apologists: Defending the Faith to a Hostile World; Institutional Consolidation Under Pressure; The Martyr's Grave and the Origins of the Cult of Saints.

episodes.title: 4. Scripture, Canon, and Authority: How the Bible Took Shape
episodes.description: The Hebrew Bible and the Question of "Old Testament"; The Formation of the New Testament Canon; Canon, Authority, and the Question Reformation Would Later Reopen; Textual Transmission: How the Words Themselves Survived.

episodes.title: 5. Core Doctrine I: God, Trinity, Incarnation, and Salvation
episodes.description: Monotheism Under Pressure: The Problem the Doctrine of the Trinity Solves; The Vocabulary of Trinitarian Definition; The Incarnation: God Become Human; Soteriology: How Does Christ's Death and Resurrection Save?.

episodes.title: 6. Core Doctrine II: Sacraments, the Eucharist, and Transubstantiation
episodes.description: What a Sacrament Is; Baptism: Incorporation and Cleansing; The Eucharist: Institution and Early Understanding; Transubstantiation: The Aristotelian Framework.

episodes.title: 7. Core Doctrine III: Sin, Grace, Purgatory, and the Afterlife
episodes.description: Original Sin: A Doctrine and Its Disputed Foundations; Grace, Merit, and the Larger Western Synthesis; Purgatory: Origins and Function; Heaven, Hell, and the Wider Eschatological Picture; Angels: The Celestial Hierarchy; The Devil: From Adversary to Cosmic Enemy.

episodes.title: 8. Church, Hierarchy, and Authority: Bishops, Councils, and Apostolic Succession
episodes.description: From Plural Leadership to Monepiscopacy; Apostolic Succession: The Theological Claim; Councils: Conciliar Authority and Its Theory; The Petrine Claim and the Question of Roman Primacy.

episodes.title: 9. Gnosticism, Marcion, and the Definition of Orthodoxy
episodes.description: The Problem of Naming; The Nag Hammadi Library and What It Changed; Marcion: A Distinct Case; Irenaeus and the Construction of Orthodoxy; The Limits of Repression and the Persistence of Gnosis.

episodes.title: 10. Constantine, Nicaea, and the Arian Controversy
episodes.description: Constantine: The Conversion and Its Historiographical Problems; The Church After Toleration: A New Set of Problems; Arius and the Controversy Before Nicaea; The Council of Nicaea, 325; The Long Aftermath: Arianism After Nicaea.

episodes.title: 11. Donatism, North Africa, and the Politics of Purity
episodes.description: North Africa and the Church Before the Schism; The Traditores and the Succession Dispute; Constantine and the Failure of Imperial Settlement; The Circumcellions: Class, Violence, and the Limits of Ecclesiastical Control; Augustine and the Turn to Coercion.

episodes.title: 12. Augustine versus Pelagius: Grace, Free Will, and a Political Church
episodes.description: Augustine of Hippo: The Mind Behind the Controversy; The Question of Free Will: Setting Up the Problem; Pelagius: The Position and Its Appeal; Augustine's Response: Grace, Predestination, and the Bound Will; The Political Dimension: From Theological Dispute to Imperial Condemnation; The Augustinian Legacy and Its Ambivalence.

episodes.title: 13. Nestorius, Cyril, and the Christological Wars: The Road to Ephesus
episodes.description: Two Schools and Their Different Instincts; Nestorius: The Man and the Controversy; Cyril of Alexandria: Theology and Power; The Council of Ephesus, 431: Procedure as Weapon; The Theological Residue of Ephesus.

episodes.title: 14. Chalcedon and the Making of the Miaphysite Churches
episodes.description: The Problem Ephesus Left Unsolved; Leo's Tome and the Western Position; The Council of Chalcedon, 451; The Miaphysite Rejection and the Permanent Schism.

episodes.title: 15. Global Spread, Phase One: Byzantium, Armenia, Ethiopia, and the Church of the East to China
episodes.description: Christianity as a Multipolar Phenomenon; Byzantium: The Christian Empire of the East; Armenia: The First Christian Nation; Ethiopia: Christianity in the Kingdom of Aksum; The Church of the East: Christianity Beyond Rome; The Significance of This Diversity.

episodes.title: 16. Monasticism: Benedict, the Desert Fathers, and the Shaping of Western Christendom
episodes.description: The Impulse and Its Context; The Desert Fathers: Egypt and the Anachoretic Tradition; Pachomius and the Cenobitic Alternative; Basil and the Eastern Synthesis; Benedict of Nursia and the Western Synthesis; The Political Economy of Monasticism; Monasticism and the Transmission of Knowledge.

episodes.title: 17. Conversion of the North: Franks, Anglo-Saxons, and the Carolingian Church
episodes.description: Conversion as Political Event; Clovis and the Frankish Conversion; Ireland and the Peregrini: Monasticism as Mission; The Anglo-Saxon Mission and the Roman Model; Charlemagne and the Carolingian Church.

episodes.title: 18. Iconoclasm and the Byzantine Crisis
episodes.description: Images and Their Contested Place in Christian Devotion; The Origins of Imperial Iconoclasm; The Course of the Controversy; Monasticism, Resistance, and the Reconfiguration of Authority; Iconoclasm and the Estrangement of Rome.

episodes.title: 19. The Filioque, Rome versus Constantinople, and the Schism of 1054
episodes.description: A Schism in Slow Motion; The Filioque: A Theological Dispute and Its History; Diverging Ecclesiologies: The Structural Incompatibility; The Photian Schism and the Ninth-Century Crisis; 1054: The Trigger and Its Limits; The Fourth Crusade's Shadow: 1204 and the Real Wound.

episodes.title: 20. Gregorian Reform and the Investiture Controversy: Church versus Empire
episodes.description: The Problem of a Church Embedded in Feudal Power; Cluny and the Monastic Origins of Reform; Leo IX and the Reform Papacy; Gregory VII: The Theology of Reform; The Investiture Contest: Henry IV and the Road to Canossa; The Longer Consequences.

episodes.title: 21. The Crusades: Origins, Aims, and the Sack of Constantinople
episodes.description: What Were the Crusades?; The Background: Holy War, Pilgrimage, and the Devotional World; Urban II at Clermont, 1095: The Appeal and Its Ambiguities; The First Crusade and Jerusalem's Fall: 1096–1099; Bernard of Clairvaux: The Conscience of the Twelfth Century; Saladin, the Loss of Jerusalem, and the Later Crusades; The Anti-Jewish Violence of the Crusades; The Crusades in Historical Perspective.

episodes.title: 22. Heresy and Repression: Cathars, the Albigensian Crusade, and the Inquisition
episodes.description: The Cathar Movement: What It Was and What It Was Not; The Political Geography of the Languedoc; The Inquisition: Origins, Methods, and Realities; The Destruction of Catharism and Its Lessons.

episodes.title: 23. Scholasticism: Aquinas and the Marriage of Faith and Reason
episodes.description: The Institutional Revolution: The Rise of the Universities; The Recovery of Aristotle and Its Consequences; Thomas Aquinas: The Synthesis; The Condemnations of 1277 and the Limits of Synthesis.

episodes.title: 24. The Church and the Jews: The Origins of Institutional Christian Antisemitism
episodes.description: Framing: Theology, History, and Moral Responsibility; The Patristic Roots: Supersessionism and the Adversus Judaeos Tradition; The Charge of Deicide and Its Consequences; The Institutional Architecture of Mediaeval Jewish Subjugation; The Black Death and the Accusations of Well-Poisoning; Forward Threads: Luther and the Holocaust.

episodes.title: 25. Avignon, Schism, and the Conciliar Crisis
episodes.description: The Road to Avignon: Boniface VIII and the Overreach of Papal Power; Avignon: The Captive Papacy?; The Great Western Schism: Three Popes and a Broken Church; The Conciliar Movement: A Constitutional Theory of Church Governance; Jan Hus and the Council's Moral Failure; The Conciliar Movement's Defeat and Its Consequences.

episodes.title: 26. Heresy Before Luther: Wycliffe, Hus, and the Limits of Dissent
episodes.description: Why These Movements Matter; John Wycliffe: Scripture, Dominion, and the Attack on the Church; Jan Hus: Bohemia and the Politicisation of Reform; Why the Limits Held — And Why They Would Not Hold for Luther.

episodes.title: 27. Luther, the Ninety-Five Theses, and the Theological Break
episodes.description: The Man and His Formation; The Indulgence Controversy and the Ninety-Five Theses; The Theological Core: Justification by Faith Alone; Sola Scriptura and the Bondage of the Will; The Diet of Worms and the Point of No Return; Luther and the Jews: The Threading Commitment.

episodes.title: 28. The Political Reformation: Princes, Peasants, and the Fragmentation of Christendom
episodes.description: The Reformation as Political Event; The Knights' Revolt and Its Lessons; The Peasants' War: 1524–1525; The Princes' Reformation: Territorial Adoption and the Emergence of Lutheran Churches; The Diet of Speyer and the Name "Protestant"; The Peace of Augsburg, 1555, and Cuius Regio Eius Religio; The Radical Reformation: Anabaptists and the Left Wing.

episodes.title: 29. Calvin, Zwingli, and the Reformed Tradition
episodes.description: Zwingli: The Swiss Reformation and Its Distinct Character; The Marburg Colloquy and the Eucharistic Division; John Calvin: Theology and Institution; Geneva as Laboratory: Discipline, Consistory, and Christian Society; The International Spread of Calvinism.

episodes.title: 30. The English Reformation: A State Church by Royal Decree
episodes.description: The Preconditions: Lollardy, Humanism, and Anti-Clericalism; Henry VIII: Jurisdiction, Marriage, and the Break with Rome; The Dissolution of the Monasteries and the Pilgrimage of Grace; Edward, Mary, and the Instability of Settlement; Cranmer, the Prayer Book, and the Shaping of Anglican Culture; The Long-Term Character of English Christianity.

episodes.title: 31. The Catholic Counter-Reformation: Trent, the Jesuits, and Discipline Restored
episodes.description: Naming the Movement; The Council of Trent: Reform and Definition; Ignatius of Loyola and the Society of Jesus; The Spanish Inquisition; The Tridentine Settlement and Its Long Shadow.

episodes.title: 32. Witch Hunts: Theology, Society, and Early Modern Persecution
episodes.description: The Historiographical Problem; The Theological Framework: What Made Witch Belief Possible; The Mechanics of Persecution: Courts, Confessions, and Chain Reactions; Geography and Confession: Who Persecuted Most, and Why; Possession, Exorcism, and the Demonological Precondition; The Decline of the Witch Trials.

episodes.title: 33. The Wars of Religion and the Peace of Westphalia
episodes.description: The Confessionalisation of Violence; The French Wars of Religion; The Thirty Years War: Europe's Catastrophe; The Peace of Westphalia and Its Mythology; The Legacy for Christianity.

episodes.title: 34. Mission and Empire: Christianity in the Americas, Africa, and Asia
episodes.description: The Inseparability of Mission and Empire; The Americas: Conquest, Conversion, and Catastrophe; Africa: Coastal Mission, Slavery, and the Interior; Asia: Ricci, the Chinese Rites, and the Limits of Accommodation; The Structural Legacy.

episodes.title: 35. The Churches and Slavery: Complicity and Abolition
episodes.description: The Scale of the Crime and the Church's Involvement; Institutional Entanglement: Churches as Slaveholders; The Abolition Movement: Christians as Agents of Change; The Theological Reckoning.

episodes.title: 36. Faith Under Siege: Enlightenment Critique, Vatican I, and the Church Against Modernity
episodes.description: The Enlightenment Challenge: What It Actually Was; The Church's Responses: Reform, Retreat, and Reaction; Darwin and the Churches; Vatican I: Papal Infallibility and Its Context; Catholic Modernism and Its Condemnation.

episodes.title: 37. The Churches and the World Wars: Complicity, Resistance, and the Reichskonkordat
episodes.description: Christianity and the First World War; The Reichskonkordat and the German Churches; Bonhoeffer, the Resistance, and the Martyrs; Pius XII and the Holocaust: A Reckoning; The Church of the East: The Assyrian Genocide and Modern Remnant; The Long Reckoning.

episodes.title: 38. Decolonisation and the New Centre of Gravity: Global South Christianity and the Rise of Pentecostalism
episodes.description: The Demographic Revolution; African Christianity After Colonialism; Latin American Christianity: Liberation and Pentecost; Pentecostalism as a Global Phenomenon; The Church of the East: Final Thread; The World Christianity Paradigm.

episodes.title: 39. Vatican II and Liberation Theology: The Church Reforms and Radicalises
episodes.description: The Rupture with the Tridentine Settlement; The Council's Achievements; The Post-Conciliar Tension: Reception and Resistance; Liberation Theology: The Preferential Option in Practice; Nostra Aetate, Antisemitism, and the Unfinished Reckoning; The Francis Pontificate and the Council's Contested Legacy.

episodes.title: 40. Reckoning: The Abuse Crisis, Secularisation, and Christianity's Global Picture Today
episodes.description: The Abuse Crisis: Institutional Failure and Its Roots; The Institutional Logic and the Theological Cost; Secularisation: The European Story and Its Limits; American Evangelical Christianity and the Political Turn; Women in the Catholic Church: Ordination, Equality, and the Legal Tension; Christianity's Global Picture: A Stocktaking.

episodes.title: Annex A: The Saints — A Reference Guide
episodes.description: What a saint is and how the cult of saints arose; the apostolic, patristic, medieval, Reformation-era and modern saints; the patron saints.

episodes.title: Annex C, part one: Christian Holidays — the Easter Cycle
episodes.description: Christian holidays in England, Ireland and Germany: the moveable feasts from Shrove Tuesday and Fastnacht to Pentecost, Trinity Sunday and Corpus Christi.

episodes.title: Annex C, part two: Christian Holidays — the Christmas Cycle and Other Feasts
episodes.description: The fixed feasts: Advent, St Nicholas, Christmas, Epiphany, Candlemas, the Assumption, All Saints and All Souls, Christ the King; and a note on denominational variation.
